![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14096165/assets/787b62fbe367feae9e4c8ed10b983a256840e3a93727fea7c1ff67cacad0129d.png)

Describe the shaded region shown above using set-builder notation.
examples.worked_solution:
Since all points $P(x,y)$ in our set lie at integer values of $x$ and $y,$ we have $x\in \mathbb Z, y\in\mathbb Z,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in \mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z = \mathbb Z^2.
$$

The points in our set include all those that lie *below* the line $y=x+2.$ For those points, the following condition is satisfied:

$$
y \lt x+2
$$

Also, notice that some points in our set lie *on* the line. We include these points by changing the inequality symbol above as follows:

$$
y \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\leq }x+2
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as follows:

$$
\Big\{(x,y) \in \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\mathbb Z ^2} \: : \: y \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\leq }x+2 \Big\}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14096165/assets/993cfa437e54f390237b85f3d7ee8a76b626d65431908fe039e0046ba0a33bb1.png)

Describe the shaded region shown above using set-builder notation.

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,3\,{{field-1}}\,x\,{{field-2}}\,6,\,1\,{{field-3}}\,y\,{{field-4}}\,4}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
A point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the rectangle if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
\begin{aligned}3<x<6,\,1<y<4.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we also need to

- *include* the left edge ($x=3$), and

- *include* the bottom edge ($y=1$).

Therefore, we change the corresponding inequality symbols to non-strict, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\le x<6,\,1\le y<4.\end{aligned}
$$

Moreover, since *every* real value in these intervals is included, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write our set as follows:

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,3\le x<6,\,1\le y<4}.
$$
